_readme: One entry per film. Times are beat names from tmp/films/<flow>/capture.json, optionally +/- seconds. Segments play in order; anything between them is cut. A segment with speed > 1 is labelled on screen with its speed and its real length. Every caption must be on screen in the app or in memory/2026-09-09-flipbrief-claim-register.md.

note.question: Will my staff actually use it?
note.title: A shift note, start to finish

captions.text:
Today shows who still
needs a note.
One tap opens it.

Answer the service plan
by tapping.

Then tap what happened
on the shift.

Tap Write my note. It drafts
from what you tapped.

Read it. Change anything
that is not right.

Type your name, or sign
on the glass.

Signed and locked,
with the time to the minute.

It cannot be edited.
A fix goes on as an addendum.

Then straight on to
the next person.

form.question: Can staff write on our own form?
form.title: Bring your own form

captions.text:
Start with the blank form
your staff already fill in.

Photos or a PDF. Here: West Virginia's
blank form, WV-BMS-IDD-7.

It reads every question
and every box.

Three forms in those pages.
Pick the one staff write on.

Shown back filled in,
with a made-up person.

Something wrong?
Fix it before anyone uses it.
Looks right? Use it.

Every new note is written on it.
Signed notes keep their form.

setup.question: Do I have to retype everyone?
setup.title: Set up in three steps

captions.text:
Three steps: your form,
your people, your staff.

Your people: paste the roster
your old system exports.

Check what it read
before anything is added.

Four people added.
Nobody retyped a thing.
Then your staff.

Their role, and the title
they sign with.

Send them the link.
It works once per person.

letterhead.question: Will it look like my agency?
letterhead.title: Your letterhead, your colours

captions.text:
This is the printed form
before you change anything.

Your legal name
and your address.
Your logo.
Your colours.

Same form.
Your agency.

Saved. New notes
print this way.
